title: Soft Scrambled Eggs on Toast
description: Low and slow is the whole trick. Take them off the heat while they still look underdone.
steps: Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt until no streaks of white remain.
Melt the butter in a nonstick pan over low heat.
Add the eggs. Stir constantly with a spatula, scraping the bottom, for 4 to 6 minutes.
Pull the pan off the heat while the eggs still look slightly wet. They carry on cooking.
Toast the bread, pile the eggs on top, and finish with pepper and sliced green onion.

title: Overnight Oats
description: Assembled in two minutes the night before, ready when you are.
steps: Stir the oats, milk, yogurt and honey together in a jar.
Add the chia seeds if using and stir again so they do not clump.
Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Top with berries before eating. Loosen with a splash more milk if it has set too thick.

title: Banana Pancakes
description: Riper bananas mean sweeter pancakes, so use the ones going spotty.
steps: Mash one banana and slice the other.
Whisk flour, baking powder, sugar and salt in a bowl.
In a second bowl, beat the eggs with the milk, melted butter and mashed banana.
Fold wet into dry until just combined. Lumps are fine; overmixing makes them tough.
Cook in a buttered pan over medium heat, about 2 minutes per side, until bubbles set on the surface.
Serve with the sliced banana and maple syrup.

title: Vegetable Omelette
description: Whatever vegetables are wilting in the drawer, cooked down first so they do not water down the eggs.
steps: Dice the pepper and slice the mushrooms.
Cook the pepper and mushrooms in the oil over medium-high heat until any liquid has evaporated, about 5 minutes.
Add the spinach and cook until just wilted. Tip everything onto a plate.
Beat the eggs with salt and pepper and pour into the same pan over medium-low heat.
When the edges set, add the vegetables and cheese to one half, fold over, and slide onto a plate.

title: Breakfast Burrito
description: Everything at once, wrapped tight enough to eat with one hand.
steps: Dice the potatoes small and fry in the oil over medium-high heat until browned and tender, 10 to 12 minutes. Salt them.
Brown the sausage in a second pan, breaking it up as it cooks.
Scramble the eggs softly in the sausage fat.
Warm the tortillas so they fold without cracking.
Layer potato, sausage, egg, cheese and salsa down the middle, fold in the sides, then roll tight.
Sear the seam side down in a dry pan for a minute to seal.

title: Yogurt and Berry Parfait
description: Three minutes, no stove, and it holds you until lunch.
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes until fragrant, then chop roughly.
Layer yogurt, berries and nuts in two glasses, twice over.
Drizzle honey on top and eat straight away so the nuts stay crisp.

title: Avocado Toast with a Fried Egg
description: Season the avocado properly. Unsalted avocado is the difference between good and dull.
steps: Toast the bread until properly crisp so it holds up.
Mash the avocado with a squeeze of lemon and a good pinch of salt.
Fry the eggs in the olive oil, spooning hot oil over the whites until set.
Spread the avocado on the toast, top with an egg each, and finish with pepper flakes.

title: Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato sauce. One pan, and bread is the only cutlery you need.
steps: Slice the onion and pepper and cook in the oil over medium heat until soft, about 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin and paprika and cook one more minute until they smell toasty.
Pour in the tomatoes, season with salt, and simmer 10 minutes until thickened.
Make six wells with the back of a spoon and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook 6 to 8 minutes, until the whites are set but the yolks still wobble.
Scatter over feta and cilantro. Serve with bread for scooping.

title: French Toast
description: Day-old bread soaks better than fresh. Slightly stale is an advantage here.
steps: Whisk eggs, milk, sugar, cinnamon and vanilla in a shallow dish.
Soak each slice 20 seconds a side. Longer for stale bread, shorter for fresh.
Cook in butter over medium heat, 2 to 3 minutes a side, until deep golden.
Keep finished slices warm in a low oven while you do the rest. Serve with syrup.

title: Potato and Sausage Hash
description: Resist stirring. The crust only forms if you leave the potatoes alone.
steps: Dice the potatoes into small cubes so they cook through quickly.
Brown the sausage in a large skillet, then lift it out, leaving the fat behind.
Add the oil and potatoes in an even layer. Leave them undisturbed 6 minutes before turning.
Add the onion and pepper and cook another 8 minutes until everything is browned and tender.
Return the sausage, season with paprika, salt and pepper.
Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover, and cook until the whites set.

title: Grilled Cheese
description: Butter the bread, not the pan, and keep the heat lower than feels right.
steps: Butter one side of each slice of bread.
Build the sandwiches butter-side out, with the cheese and a smear of mustard inside.
Cook over medium-low heat, pressing gently, 3 to 4 minutes a side.
Low heat is the point: it gives the cheese time to melt before the bread burns.

title: Chicken Caesar Salad
description: The dressing comes together in a jar while the chicken rests.
steps: Season the chicken and sear in the oil over medium-high heat, 5 to 6 minutes a side. Rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Mash the anchovies and garlic to a paste. Whisk with mayonnaise, lemon juice, mustard and half the parmesan.
If making croutons, cube the bread and toast in a little oil until crisp.
Chop the romaine, toss with the dressing, and top with chicken, remaining parmesan and croutons.

title: Tuna Salad Sandwich
description: Celery is what keeps this from being one soft texture.
steps: Drain the tuna thoroughly. Wet tuna makes a soggy sandwich.
Finely dice the celery and onion.
Mix everything with the mayonnaise, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Pile onto bread with a lettuce leaf underneath to keep it from going soft.

title: Caprese Sandwich
description: Only worth making when the tomatoes are actually good.
steps: Slice the tomatoes and mozzarella thickly. Salt the tomato slices and leave them 5 minutes.
Drizzle the bread with olive oil, or spread with pesto.
Layer mozzarella, tomato and basil. Finish with balsamic and a grind of pepper.

title: Smashed Chickpea Wrap
description: Same idea as tuna salad, but from a can of chickpeas you already own.
steps: Drain and rinse the chickpeas, then smash roughly with a fork. Leave some texture.
Dice the celery and onion finely and fold in with the mayonnaise, mustard and lemon.
Season well, taste, and adjust the lemon.
Roll up in tortillas with a lettuce leaf.

title: Quinoa Power Bowl
description: Rinse the quinoa first unless you like it bitter.
steps: Rinse the quinoa well, then simmer in twice its volume of salted water for 15 minutes. Rest covered 5 minutes and fluff.
Meanwhile cube the sweet potato, toss with oil, cumin and salt, and roast at 425F for 25 minutes.
Drain the chickpeas and roast alongside for the last 15 minutes so they crisp.
Thin the tahini with lemon juice and a little water until pourable.
Build bowls with quinoa, spinach, sweet potato, chickpeas and sliced avocado. Spoon over the dressing.

title: BLT
description: Toast the bread. An untoasted BLT collapses.
steps: Cook the bacon in a cold pan brought up to medium heat, turning until evenly crisp. Drain on paper.
Toast the bread.
Slice the tomato and season the slices with salt and pepper.
Spread mayonnaise on both slices, then layer lettuce, tomato and bacon. Lettuce goes against the bread to keep it dry.

title: Egg Fried Rice
description: Cold leftover rice only. Fresh rice steams instead of frying.
steps: Use rice cooked the day before and chilled. Break up any clumps with your fingers.
Scramble the eggs in a little oil in a very hot wok or wide pan, then set aside.
Add the rest of the oil and fry the diced carrot 2 minutes, then the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the rice and press it into the pan. Leave it 1 minute at a time between stirs so it catches.
Return the egg, add the peas and soy sauce, and toss until heated through.
Off the heat, add the sesame oil and sliced green onion.

title: Minestrone
description: A soup designed around whatever vegetables need using up.
steps: Dice the onion, carrot and celery and sweat in the oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until soft but not coloured.
Add the garlic and Italian seasoning, cook 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, broth and beans. Simmer 20 minutes.
Add the diced zucchini and pasta and cook until the pasta is done, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the spinach until wilted. Taste for salt, which this needs more of than you expect.
Serve with grated parmesan.

title: Lentil Soup
description: Cheap, filling, and better the next day.
steps: Sweat the diced onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 10 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin and paprika and cook until fragrant.
Add the lentils, tomatoes and broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer 30 to 35 minutes until the lentils are soft.
Blend about a third of the soup and stir it back in for body.
Finish with lemon juice off the heat. This is what makes it taste finished rather than flat.

title: Greek Salad
description: No lettuce. Salt the tomatoes early and use the juice as part of the dressing.
steps: Cut the tomatoes into wedges, salt them, and leave 10 minutes.
Cut the cucumber into thick half moons and slice the onion thinly.
Combine everything with the olives, keeping the tomato juices.
Dress with oil, vinegar and oregano. Lay the feta on top in a slab rather than crumbling it.

title: Turkey Club
description: Three slices of bread, which is what makes it a club rather than a sandwich.
steps: Crisp the bacon and toast all six slices of bread.
Spread mayonnaise on every toasted surface that will face a filling.
Build the first layer with turkey or ham and cheese, add the middle slice, then bacon, lettuce and tomato.
Press down, spear with cocktail sticks at the corners, and cut into quarters diagonally.

title: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
description: Five ingredients. The pasta water is one of them, and it is not optional.
steps: Boil the pasta in well salted water. Reserve a mug of the water before draining.
While it cooks, slice the garlic thinly and warm it in the oil over low heat until pale gold. Do not let it brown or it turns bitter.
Add the pepper flakes and take the pan off the heat.
Add the drained pasta to the oil with a splash of pasta water and toss hard until the sauce turns glossy and clings.
Add more pasta water if it looks dry. Finish with parsley.

title: Spaghetti Bolognese
description: The milk is not a mistake. It tenderises the meat before the tomatoes go in.
steps: Finely dice onion, carrot and celery and cook in the oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until soft.
Add the beef, breaking it up, and brown properly. Let the liquid cook off before you move on.
Add the milk and simmer until almost gone. Then the wine, and again until almost gone.
Stir in the tomato paste, cook 1 minute, then add the tomatoes, bay leaf and salt.
Simmer uncovered on the lowest heat for at least an hour, stirring now and then.
Cook the spaghetti, toss it with the sauce and a splash of pasta water, and serve with parmesan.

title: Chicken Parmesan
description: Pound the cutlets thin so they cook through before the crust burns.
steps: Halve the breasts horizontally and pound to an even half inch.
Set up three dishes: seasoned flour, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs mixed with parmesan and garlic powder.
Coat each cutlet in flour, egg, then crumbs, pressing firmly.
Fry in the oil over medium-high heat, 3 minutes a side, until deep golden. Drain briefly.
Spoon sauce into a baking dish, lay the cutlets on top, then more sauce and the mozzarella.
Bake at 425F for 12 minutes until bubbling. Keeping the sauce off the crust is what stops it going soft.

title: Garlic Butter Chicken
description: One pan, twenty minutes, and the sauce makes itself from the fond.
steps: Pat the chicken dry and season well. Dry skin is what browns.
Sear in the oil over medium-high heat, 6 minutes a side, until cooked through. Move to a plate.
Lower the heat, add the butter and sliced garlic, and cook 1 minute until fragrant but not brown.
Pour in the broth and scrape up everything stuck to the pan.
Simmer 2 minutes to thicken slightly, add lemon juice and thyme, then return the chicken and any juices.
Spoon the sauce over and scatter with parsley.

title: Chicken Stir Fry
description: Have everything chopped before the pan gets hot. There is no time once it starts.
steps: Start the rice first.
Slice the chicken thinly and toss with 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce and the cornstarch.
Cut all the vegetables to a similar size. Mix the remaining soy sauce with 3 tablespoons water.
Get the pan very hot. Sear the chicken in one layer without moving it for 2 minutes, then stir until just cooked. Remove.
Add the vegetables, hardest first, and stir fry 4 minutes. They should stay crunchy.
Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, return the chicken, pour in the sauce, and toss until it thickens and coats. Finish with sesame oil.

title: Beef and Broccoli
description: Slicing the beef against the grain matters more than the cut you buy.
steps: Start the rice.
Slice the beef thinly across the grain and toss with 1 tablespoon soy sauce and 1 tablespoon cornstarch.
Mix the remaining soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, remaining cornstarch and half a cup of water.
Blanch the broccoli in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain well.
Sear the beef in a very hot pan in two batches so it browns rather than steams. Remove.
Cook the garlic and ginger 30 seconds, return the beef and broccoli, add the sauce and toss until glossy.

title: Pad Thai
description: Soak the noodles, do not boil them. Boiled rice noodles turn to paste in the wok.
steps: Soak the noodles in hot tap water 20 minutes until pliable but still firm. Drain.
Mix the fish sauce, sugar and the juice of one lime into a sauce.
Heat the oil until shimmering. Cook the shrimp 2 minutes until pink, then remove.
Add the garlic, then push aside and scramble the eggs in the space.
Add the drained noodles and the sauce. Toss constantly for 3 minutes until the noodles absorb it.
Return the shrimp, add the green onion, and serve with crushed peanuts and the second lime cut into wedges.

title: Chicken Curry
description: Bloom the spices in oil before the liquid goes in. Skipping that step makes it taste raw.
steps: Brown the chicken pieces in the oil in batches, then set aside.
Cook the diced onion in the same pan for 8 minutes until golden at the edges.
Add the garlic, ginger and all the dry spices. Stir for 1 minute until they darken and smell toasted.
Add the tomatoes and cook down 5 minutes, then the coconut milk.
Return the chicken and simmer 20 minutes uncovered until the sauce coats a spoon.
Salt to taste and finish with cilantro. Serve over rice.

title: Thai Green Curry
description: Fry the paste in the thick coconut cream first. That step is where the flavour comes from.
steps: Open the coconut milk without shaking and spoon the thick cream from the top into a hot pan.
Fry the curry paste in that cream for 3 minutes until the oil separates and it darkens.
Add the sliced chicken and coat it in the paste.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk, add fish sauce and sugar, and simmer 12 minutes.
Add the sliced pepper and zucchini and cook 6 more minutes so they keep some bite.
Off the heat, add lime juice and basil. Serve with rice.

title: Chana Masala
description: Almost entirely from cans and jars, which is what makes it a good Tuesday.
steps: Cook the finely diced onion in the oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until properly golden. Rushing this costs you flavour.
Add garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander and turmeric. Stir 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes until the oil separates out again.
Add the drained chickpeas and a cup of water. Simmer 15 minutes.
Mash a few chickpeas against the side of the pan to thicken the sauce.
Stir in garam masala, salt and lemon juice. Finish with cilantro.

title: Black Bean Tacos
description: Ten minutes from a can to the table, and better than that sounds.
steps: Cook the diced onion in the oil for 6 minutes, then add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the drained beans with a splash of water and cook 5 minutes, mashing about half of them.
Season with salt and lime juice.
Char the tortillas directly over a flame or in a dry pan until they blister.
Fill and top with avocado, cheese and cilantro.

title: Beef Tacos
description: Drain the fat before the seasoning goes in or the filling turns greasy.
steps: Brown the beef with the diced onion over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it goes.
Tip off the rendered fat.
Add the seasoning and a third of a cup of water. Simmer 5 minutes until it thickens and clings.
Warm the tortillas until soft and pliable.
Set out the shredded lettuce, diced tomato, cheese and lime and let everyone build their own.

title: Chicken Fajitas
description: Get the pan properly hot. Fajitas want char, not a gentle sauté.
steps: Slice the chicken, peppers and onion into strips of roughly equal width.
Toss the chicken with the spices, garlic, salt, half the oil and the juice of one lime. Leave 10 minutes.
Sear the chicken in a screaming hot pan in a single layer, 3 minutes without touching it, then turn. Remove.
Add the rest of the oil and cook the peppers and onion hard for 5 minutes until charred at the edges but still crisp.
Return the chicken, squeeze over the second lime, and serve with warm tortillas.

title: Sheet Pan Salmon and Vegetables
description: The vegetables get a head start because salmon needs far less time than they do.
steps: Heat the oven to 425F.
Cube the potatoes, toss with half the oil and salt, and roast 20 minutes on their own.
Add the broccoli florets, tossed in oil, and push everything to the edges.
Lay the salmon in the middle, brush with the rest of the oil, garlic and thyme, and season.
Roast 12 to 14 minutes until the salmon flakes at the thickest part. Squeeze lemon over everything.

title: Shrimp Scampi
description: The shrimp take three minutes. Everything else should be ready before they go in.
steps: Boil the pasta and save a mug of the water.
Cook the sliced garlic and pepper flakes gently in the oil for 1 minute.
Add the wine and reduce by half.
Add the shrimp in one layer and cook 90 seconds a side, until just pink. Any longer and they go rubbery.
Take the pan off the heat and swirl in the butter and lemon juice until the sauce emulsifies.
Toss with the drained pasta and enough pasta water to keep it loose. Finish with parsley.

title: Fish Tacos
description: A quick slaw does two jobs here: crunch, and something acidic against the fried fish.
steps: Shred the cabbage finely and toss with the juice of one lime and a pinch of salt. Leave it to soften while you cook.
Mix the mayonnaise with sriracha and a squeeze of lime for the sauce.
Cut the fish into strips, season with cumin, chili powder and salt.
Fry in the oil over medium-high heat, 2 to 3 minutes a side, until it flakes.
Char the tortillas, then build with fish, slaw, sauce, avocado and cilantro.

title: Mushroom Risotto
description: Keep the stock hot and add it slowly. Cold stock stops the cooking each time.
steps: Keep the broth at a bare simmer in a separate pan throughout.
Brown the sliced mushrooms hard in the oil, in batches so they colour rather than steam. Set aside and salt them.
Soften the diced onion in the same pan, add the garlic, then the rice. Toast the rice 2 minutes until the edges look translucent.
Add the wine and stir until it has gone.
Add hot broth one ladle at a time, stirring, waiting until each is nearly absorbed before the next. About 20 minutes.
When the rice is creamy but still has a slight bite, take it off the heat and beat in the butter, parmesan and mushrooms. Rest 2 minutes before serving.

title: Butternut Squash Soup
description: Roasting rather than boiling the squash is the whole difference.
steps: Halve the squash, scoop out the seeds, rub with oil and salt, and roast cut side down at 425F for 40 minutes.
Meanwhile soften the onion, carrot and garlic in the rest of the oil.
Scoop the roasted flesh into the pot, add the broth and spices, and simmer 10 minutes.
Blend until completely smooth. Take your time here; a grainy squash soup is a disappointing one.
Stir in the cream, then salt aggressively until it stops tasting flat.

title: Beef Stew
description: Brown the meat in batches. Crowding the pan gives you grey beef and no fond.
steps: Cube the beef, pat it dry, and toss with the flour, salt and pepper.
Brown in the oil in three batches over high heat. Do not crowd the pan. Set each batch aside.
Cook the onion, carrot and celery in the same pot until softened, then add garlic and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes.
Add the wine and scrape the bottom clean.
Return the beef, add the broth, bay and thyme, and simmer covered on low for 90 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cook another 40 minutes until the beef pulls apart with a spoon.

title: Chili con Carne
description: Better on day two, so make more than you need.
steps: Brown the beef hard, then drain off the excess fat.
Add the diced onion and pepper and cook 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, chili powder, cumin and paprika, and stir 1 minute in the hot fat to bloom them.
Add the tomato paste, tomatoes, drained beans and broth.
Simmer uncovered at least 45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick enough that a spoon leaves a trail.
Salt to taste. Serve with cheese and sour cream.

title: Stovetop Mac and Cheese
description: Take the pan off the heat before the cheese goes in or the sauce will split.
steps: Boil the pasta one minute short of the packet time and drain.
Melt the butter, whisk in the flour, and cook 1 minute without letting it colour.
Add the milk gradually, whisking, and simmer until it thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Take the pan off the heat. Only now add the grated cheese, a handful at a time, stirring until smooth.
Season with mustard, salt and pepper, then fold in the pasta.
For a crust, top with breadcrumbs and parmesan and grill for 3 minutes.

title: Lasagna
description: Let it rest twenty minutes out of the oven or the slices will slide apart.
steps: Brown the beef with the onion, add garlic and seasoning, then the tomatoes. Simmer 30 minutes.
Mix the ricotta with the egg, half the parmesan and a good pinch of salt.
Cook the noodles if they are not the no-boil kind, and lay them out flat so they do not stick.
Layer: sauce, noodles, ricotta, mozzarella. Repeat three times, finishing with sauce and cheese.
Cover with foil and bake at 375F for 40 minutes, then uncover for 20 more until browned and bubbling.
Rest 20 minutes before cutting. This step is not optional.

title: Pesto Pasta
description: Never heat pesto directly. Loosen it with pasta water off the heat instead.
steps: Boil the pasta in well salted water. Reserve a mug of water before draining.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan until golden. Watch them; they burn in seconds.
Halve the tomatoes and warm briefly in the oil.
Off the heat, toss the drained pasta with the pesto and a few tablespoons of pasta water until it coats every piece.
Fold in the tomatoes and spinach, and top with parmesan and pine nuts.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
description: No cream. The sauce is egg, cheese and pasta water, and the pan must be off the heat.
steps: Beat the eggs with the grated parmesan and a lot of black pepper. It should look like a thick paste.
Cook the diced bacon slowly until crisp, leaving the fat in the pan.
Boil the pasta and save two mugs of the water.
Take the pan completely off the heat. Add the drained pasta and toss in the fat.
Wait thirty seconds, then add the egg mixture and toss hard, adding pasta water until it turns into a glossy sauce.
If the pan is too hot you get scrambled egg. Off the heat and keep moving is the whole technique.

title: Roast Chicken with Vegetables
description: Dry the skin and salt it early. That is most of what makes it crisp.
steps: Pat the chicken very dry, salt it all over, and leave it uncovered in the fridge for an hour if you have time.
Heat the oven to 425F. Cut the vegetables into large chunks and toss with oil, thyme and salt in a roasting tin.
Put the halved lemon and the garlic head inside the cavity, rub the skin with oil, and set the bird on top of the vegetables.
Roast 70 to 80 minutes, until a thigh reads 165F and the juices run clear.
Rest the chicken 15 minutes before carving. Toss the vegetables in the pan juices while it rests.

title: Pork Chops with Apples
description: Pull the chops at 145F. Pork does not need to be cooked to grey.
steps: Season the chops well and let them sit at room temperature 15 minutes.
Sear in the oil over medium-high heat, 4 to 5 minutes a side, until they read 145F. Rest on a plate.
Melt the butter and cook the sliced onion and apple wedges for 6 minutes until they take on colour.
Add the broth, vinegar, mustard and thyme, and simmer until slightly syrupy.
Return the chops and any resting juices to the pan and spoon the sauce over.

title: Teriyaki Salmon
description: Glaze at the end, not the start, or the sugar burns before the fish is done.
steps: Start the rice.
Simmer the soy sauce, sugar, ginger, garlic and vinegar for 3 minutes, then whisk in the cornstarch slurried with a tablespoon of water. It should thicken to a glaze.
Pat the salmon dry and sear skin side down in the oil for 5 minutes, then flip for 3 more.
Spoon the glaze over the fish in the last minute and let it bubble and cling.
Serve over rice with green onion and sesame seeds.

title: Pork Fried Rice
description: A use for last night's rice and whatever pork is left.
steps: Use cold cooked rice and break up the clumps first.
Brown the pork in a very hot pan, then push it to one side and scramble the eggs in the space.
Add the diced carrot, garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute.
Add the rice and press it flat. Let it sit a minute between stirs so it toasts.
Add the peas, soy sauce and oyster sauce and toss until evenly coloured.
Finish off the heat with sesame oil and green onion.

title: Miso Ramen Bowl
description: Never boil miso. Whisk it in at the end so it keeps its flavour.
steps: Boil the eggs for exactly 7 minutes, then cool in ice water and peel. The yolk should still be soft.
Cook the garlic and ginger in the sesame oil for 1 minute, then add the broth and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the sliced mushrooms and halved bok choy and cook 4 minutes.
Whisk the miso with a ladle of hot broth in a bowl until smooth, then stir it back into the pot. Do not let it boil after this.
Cook the noodles separately so they do not cloud the broth, then divide between bowls.
Ladle over the broth and vegetables, and top with a halved egg and green onion.

title: Stuffed Peppers
description: Par-bake the peppers first so they are tender when the filling is ready.
steps: Cook the rice.
Halve the peppers lengthwise, remove the seeds, rub with oil, and bake cut side up at 375F for 20 minutes.
Brown the beef with the onion, add garlic and seasoning, then the tomatoes. Simmer 10 minutes.
Fold the cooked rice into the meat and season well.
Fill the peppers, top with cheese, and bake 20 minutes until browned and bubbling.

title: Shepherd's Pie
description: Rough up the mash with a fork before it goes in. Those ridges are what crisp.
steps: Boil the peeled potatoes until fully tender, then mash with the butter, milk and plenty of salt.
Brown the beef, add the diced onion and carrot, and cook 8 minutes.
Stir in the flour and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes, then add the broth, worcestershire and thyme.
Simmer until thick, about 10 minutes, then stir in the peas and season.
Spread the meat in a baking dish, top with mash, and rough the surface with a fork.
Bake at 400F for 25 minutes until the peaks are browned.

title: Eggplant Parmesan
description: Salt the eggplant and let it drain. Otherwise the dish turns watery.
steps: Slice the eggplant into half inch rounds, salt both sides, and leave in a colander 30 minutes. Pat dry.
Set up flour, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs mixed with half the parmesan.
Coat each slice and fry in the oil until golden, about 2 minutes a side. Drain on paper.
Layer sauce, eggplant, mozzarella and parmesan in a baking dish, twice over.
Bake at 400F for 30 minutes until bubbling. Rest 10 minutes and finish with basil.

title: Crispy Tofu Stir Fry
description: Press the tofu and coat it in cornstarch. That is the difference between crisp and soggy.
steps: Press the tofu between paper towels under a weight for 15 minutes, then cube it.
Toss the cubes in cornstarch until evenly dusted.
Fry in half the oil over medium-high heat, turning only when each side has browned. Set aside.
Stir fry the broccoli and pepper in the remaining oil for 4 minutes, then add the garlic and ginger.
Mix the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and a splash of water, pour it in, and let it thicken.
Return the tofu, toss once, and serve immediately over rice before it softens.

title: Red Lentil Dal
description: The tempered spices poured over at the end are the whole point. Do not skip them.
steps: Rinse the lentils until the water runs clear.
Simmer them with the turmeric and 4 cups of water for 20 minutes until collapsing, skimming any foam.
Meanwhile cook the diced onion in the oil until golden, then add garlic, ginger, cumin and coriander for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes.
Stir the mixture into the lentils, add salt, and simmer 5 more minutes.
Finish with garam masala and lemon juice. Serve with rice and cilantro.

title: Cauliflower and Chickpea Curry
description: Roast the cauliflower separately so it keeps texture instead of dissolving into the sauce.
steps: Toss the cauliflower florets in half the oil and salt and roast at 425F for 25 minutes until browned at the edges.
Cook the diced onion in the rest of the oil for 8 minutes, then add garlic, ginger, curry powder and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook down 5 minutes, then the coconut milk and drained chickpeas.
Simmer 12 minutes until thickened.
Fold in the roasted cauliflower and the spinach at the very end so the florets keep their edges.

title: Smash Burgers
description: Smash once, hard, in the first ten seconds. After that, leave it alone.
steps: Divide the beef into four loose balls. Do not compact them.
Mix the mayonnaise, ketchup and mustard for the sauce. Toast the buns in butter.
Get a heavy pan or griddle as hot as it will go.
Put a ball on the dry surface and smash it flat with a stiff spatula within ten seconds. Season.
Cook 2 minutes until the edges are lacy and brown, flip once, add cheese, and cook 1 more minute.
Build with sauce, pickles and thin raw onion.

title: Chicken Noodle Soup
description: Cook the noodles separately if you plan on leftovers, or they drink the broth overnight.
steps: Sweat the diced onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, thyme and bay, then the broth and the whole chicken thighs.
Simmer 25 minutes, then lift out the chicken, shred it, and return it to the pot.
Cook the noodles separately and add them to each bowl rather than the pot.
Season heavily. Soup needs more salt than you think. A squeeze of lemon at the end lifts it.

title: Tomato Soup
description: A pinch of sugar balances the acid in canned tomatoes. It will not taste sweet.
steps: Cook the diced onion in the butter and oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until soft and sweet.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the tomatoes, broth, sugar and dried basil.
Simmer 20 minutes.
Blend until smooth, then stir in the cream off the heat.
Taste and salt until the flavour sharpens. Finish with torn basil.

title: Hummus
description: Ice water whipped in at the end is what makes it fluffy rather than dense.
steps: Blend the lemon juice and garlic first and let it sit 5 minutes, then strain out the garlic solids if you want it milder.
Add the tahini and blend until it seizes and pales.
Add the drained chickpeas, cumin and salt and blend 2 full minutes.
With the motor running, drizzle in 3 tablespoons of ice water until it turns pale and fluffy.
Spread in a bowl, pool olive oil in the centre, and dust with paprika.

title: Guacamole
description: Mash half and dice the rest. Uniform guacamole is a missed opportunity.
steps: Finely dice the onion and jalapeno and mash them with the salt and lime juice first. This softens the onion's bite.
Mash half the avocado into the mixture until smooth.
Dice the remaining avocado and fold it in whole so there is texture.
Stir in the cilantro and diced tomato. Taste for salt and lime, which it almost always needs more of.

title: Caprese Salad
description: Three ingredients, so all three have to be good.
steps: Slice the tomatoes and mozzarella to the same thickness.
Alternate them on a platter, tucking basil leaves between.
Salt the tomatoes specifically, not the whole plate.
Drizzle with oil, grind over pepper, and add balsamic if you like. Serve at room temperature, never cold.

title: Roasted Vegetables
description: Give them room. A crowded tray steams instead of roasting.
steps: Heat the oven to 425F and put the empty tray in to heat with it.
Cut everything to a similar size so it cooks evenly. Halve the sprouts.
Toss with oil, thyme, salt and pepper.
Spread on the hot tray in a single layer with space between pieces.
Roast 30 to 35 minutes, turning once, until the edges are properly browned. Finish with balsamic.

title: Garlic Bread
description: Raw garlic in soft butter, not garlic powder. It is a different dish.
steps: Soften the butter fully. Cold butter will tear the bread.
Grate or finely mince the garlic and mash it into the butter with the parsley and salt.
Split the loaf lengthwise and spread the butter right to the edges.
Bake at 400F for 10 minutes, then broil 2 minutes for colour. Watch it closely at that point.

title: Honey Garlic Chicken Thighs
description: Start skin side down in a cold pan and let the fat render out slowly.
steps: Season the thighs and lay them skin side down in a cold ovenproof pan. Turn the heat to medium.
Let them render 12 to 15 minutes without moving until the skin is deep gold and crisp.
Flip, then pour off most of the fat.
Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the honey, soy sauce, vinegar and pepper flakes.
Transfer to a 400F oven for 12 minutes, basting once, until the glaze is sticky and the chicken is cooked through.

title: Tuna and Tomato Pasta
description: Entirely from the cupboard, which is the point of it.
steps: Boil the pasta in well salted water and reserve a mug of the water.
Warm the sliced garlic and pepper flakes in the oil until fragrant but not coloured.
Add the tomatoes, capers and olives and simmer 10 minutes.
Flake in the drained tuna and warm through gently. Stirring hard turns it to paste.
Toss with the pasta and enough pasta water to loosen. Finish with parsley.

title: Vegetable Frittata
description: Finish it under the broiler rather than flipping. Far less can go wrong.
steps: Dice the potato small and cook in the oil in an ovenproof skillet for 10 minutes until tender.
Add the sliced onion and cook 5 more minutes, then wilt in the spinach.
Beat the eggs with the milk, parmesan, salt and pepper.
Pour over the vegetables and cook on low, undisturbed, for 8 minutes until the edges set.
Finish under a hot broiler for 3 minutes until puffed and just set in the middle. Rest 5 minutes before slicing.

title: Greek Chicken Bowls
description: The yogurt marinade tenderises as well as seasons, so give it the full half hour.
steps: Mix half the yogurt with the juice of one lemon, the garlic, oregano, oil and salt. Marinate the cubed chicken at least 30 minutes.
Prepare the couscous with hot broth or water and fluff with a fork.
Dice the cucumber, tomato and onion into a rough salad and dress with the second lemon and a little oil.
Sear the chicken in a hot pan until charred at the edges and cooked through, about 8 minutes.
Build bowls with couscous, chicken, salad, feta and a spoonful of the remaining plain yogurt.

title: Sausage and Peppers Pasta
description: Brown the sausage in chunks rather than crumbs so you get real texture.
steps: Brown the sausage in large pieces in the oil, then remove and slice into coins.
Cook the sliced peppers and onion in the fat for 8 minutes until softened and browning.
Add the garlic and pepper flakes, then the tomatoes. Simmer 10 minutes.
Return the sausage. Meanwhile boil the pasta and save some water.
Toss everything together with a splash of pasta water and finish with parmesan and basil.

title: Salmon Rice Bowl
description: Works just as well with salmon left over from the night before.
steps: Cook the rice, then fold through the rice vinegar while it is still warm.
Pat the salmon dry, season, and sear in the oil 4 minutes a side. Flake into large pieces.
Mix the mayonnaise and sriracha for the sauce.
Slice the cucumber thinly and the avocado into wedges.
Build bowls with rice, salmon, cucumber and avocado. Drizzle with the sauce, soy sauce and sesame oil.

title: White Beans with Greens
description: Fifteen minutes, almost all from the cupboard, and genuinely good.
steps: Warm the sliced garlic and pepper flakes in the oil over low heat until the garlic is pale gold.
Strip the kale from its stems, chop, and add with a splash of water. Cook until wilted.
Add the drained beans and broth and simmer 8 minutes.
Mash some of the beans against the pan to thicken the liquid into a sauce.
Finish with lemon juice and salt. Serve over toast rubbed with a cut garlic clove.

title: Chicken Quesadillas
description: Cheese on both sides of the filling is what glues it together.
steps: Slice the chicken thin and cook with the seasoning in half the oil until done. Set aside.
Cook the sliced pepper and onion in the same pan until soft and lightly charred.
Lay a tortilla in a dry pan, cover half with cheese, then filling, then more cheese, and fold over.
Cook 3 minutes a side over medium heat until the tortilla is crisp and the cheese has melted through.
Rest 2 minutes before cutting or the filling runs out. Serve with salsa and sour cream.

title: Baked Ziti
description: Undercook the pasta by two minutes. It finishes in the oven.
steps: Boil the pasta two minutes short of the packet time and drain.
Brown the beef with the onion, add garlic and seasoning, then the tomatoes. Simmer 15 minutes.
Combine the pasta with the sauce and half the mozzarella.
Layer half into a baking dish, dot with all the ricotta, then the rest of the pasta.
Top with the remaining mozzarella and the parmesan and bake at 400F for 25 minutes until browned.

title: Cold Sesame Noodles
description: Rinse the noodles cold so they stop cooking and the sauce clings.
steps: Cook the noodles, then rinse under cold water until completely cool and drain well.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, honey, grated garlic and ginger with 3 tablespoons of warm water until pourable.
Julienne the cucumber and slice the green onion.
Toss the noodles with the sauce until evenly coated, adding water a splash at a time if it stiffens.
Top with cucumber, green onion and crushed peanuts.

title: Steak Fajita Salad
description: Rest the steak before slicing or the juice ends up on the board instead of the salad.
steps: Rub the steak with cumin, chili powder, salt and a little oil.
Sear in a very hot pan 3 to 4 minutes a side for medium rare. Rest at least 8 minutes.
Char the sliced peppers and onion hard in the same pan.
Whisk the remaining oil with the juice of both limes and a pinch of salt.
Slice the steak against the grain, pile everything over the chopped romaine, and dress.

title: Potato Leek Soup
description: Wash the leeks properly. Grit in the soup cannot be fixed later.
steps: Slice the white and pale green parts of the leeks and wash them in a bowl of water, lifting them out so the grit stays behind.
Sweat the leeks in the butter over low heat for 12 minutes without letting them colour.
Add the garlic, then the cubed potatoes, broth and bay leaf.
Simmer 20 minutes until the potatoes fall apart when pressed.
Remove the bay leaf and blend until smooth. Stir in the cream and season generously.

title: Zucchini Fritters
description: Squeeze the grated zucchini until it stops giving up water, then squeeze again.
steps: Grate the zucchini, toss with 1 teaspoon of salt, and leave in a colander 15 minutes.
Wring it out in a clean towel. You should get out a surprising amount of water.
Mix with the eggs, flour, crumbled feta, green onion, dill and garlic.
Fry heaped spoonfuls in the oil over medium heat, 3 minutes a side, flattening slightly.
Drain on paper and serve with yogurt.

title: Lemon Chicken and Rice Soup
description: Temper the egg with hot broth slowly or you will end up with soup and scrambled egg.
steps: Sweat the diced onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 8 minutes.
Add the broth and the chicken and simmer 20 minutes. Lift out the chicken and shred it.
Add the rice and cook 15 minutes until tender.
Whisk the eggs with the juice of both lemons in a bowl.
Ladle hot broth into the eggs one spoonful at a time, whisking constantly, until the bowl is warm. Then pour it all back into the pot off the heat.
Return the chicken, season well, and finish with dill. Do not boil it after the egg goes in.

title: Apple Crumble
description: Cold butter rubbed in by hand gives a far better crumble than melted.
steps: Peel and slice the apples and toss with the white sugar, half the cinnamon and the lemon juice.
Rub the cold cubed butter into the flour, oats, brown sugar, salt and remaining cinnamon with your fingertips until it clumps.
Tip the apples into a baking dish and scatter the crumble over without pressing it down.
Bake at 375F for 45 minutes until the top is deep golden and the fruit bubbles at the edges.
Rest 15 minutes before serving.
